newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes flat with WTI, sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes flat with WTI, sluggish trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices were flat Wednesday, reacting to unchanged West Texas Intermediate (WTI) markets and sluggish trade talk, traders said.
Trade got a slow start in western spot markets, as players returned from an out-of-state refinery conference Wednesday
Discounts for light grades were unchanged from Friday, with Alaska North Slope (ANS) last done at -$0.91 cents off WTI. Line 63 prices were idle at postings plus $0.95 to $1.00.
Outright ANS prices stayed at Tuesday's level of $20.99/21.19 a barrel.
Nominations were due Wednesday for April shipments on Canada's Trans Mountain Pipe Line Co, a pipeline official said earlier.
Outright prices for Kern River rose late Tuesday after oil companies raised postings 50 cents The grade increased to $14.88/14.98 a barrel.
